binders: There exists a real constant c, chosen before and independently of all subsequent data.
Universally quantified types ι and Ω, where ι has a Fintype structure and Ω has a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
A finite indexed family X : ι → Ω → Real.
A proof that the universal finite set of indices is nonempty.
A universally quantified real parameter λ.
A locally defined real K equal to max_{i∈ι} (LocalDef001 μ (X_i)).toReal.
hypotheses: Every X_i is integrable with respect to μ and has integral zero.
For every i, LocalDef001 μ (X_i) is strictly below ENNReal infinity.
The indexed family X is jointly independent with respect to μ.
conclusions: For every index i, the real-valued function ω ↦ exp(λ X_i(ω)) is integrable with respect to μ.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 μ X is the ENNReal infimum of the set of LocalDef002-admissible scales.
LocalDef002 μ X t means: X is measurable; t is neither zero nor infinity; ω ↦ exp(|X(ω)|/t.toReal) is μ-integrable; and its μ-integral is at most 2.
K = max_{i∈ι} (LocalDef001 μ (X_i)).toReal, where the maximum is taken over the nonempty finite index set.
Integrable means almost-everywhere strong measurability together with finite integral norm.
iIndepFun expresses joint independence of the indexed family under μ.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive real constant c such that, for every nonempty finite family of jointly independent, measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables on an arbitrary probability space, if every variable has finite LocalDef001 gauge, then for every real λ the following holds. Let K be the maximum of the real values of those gauges. If K > 0 and |λ| ≤ c/K, then each exponential moment function exp(λ X_i) is integrable.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type must be finite and nonempty; empty families are excluded.
The same c must work uniformly for every index type, probability space, family, and λ.
The conclusion is conditional on K > 0. For a family with K = 0, the implication is vacuous after K is defined.
Each LocalDef001 value must be finite before conversion to Real; this excludes any index with gauge equal to ENNReal infinity.
The λ range is closed and two-sided: both positive and negative λ are permitted when |λ| ≤ c/K.
The conclusion asserts only integrability of exp(λ X_i), separately for each i; it gives no numerical moment bound.
Joint independence and zero means are explicit antecedents even though the conclusion concerns each individual exponential separately.
Measurability and integrability of every X_i are separately required in addition to finite LocalDef001.
Because all family conditions occur as antecedents, the assertion is trivially true for data failing any antecedent.
ambiguities: The dossier gives an exact definition of LocalDef001 but no conventional mathematical name for it; it is therefore described only by its defining infimum.

The behavior of LocalDef001 on an empty admissible-scale set is inherited from the ENNReal set-infimum structure rather than stated directly, although the theorem separately assumes every resulting gauge is finite.
The proposition does not state whether the assumptions of independence or zero mean are logically necessary for the integrability conclusion; it only includes them as hypotheses.
